create.title: Target-scale lower-profile flattening and sharp character-divisor discrepancy reduction
create.statement_tex: Let R=X^(1/4), y=floor(sqrt X), D_j=2^(-j)y, H_j=floor(D_j/R), and choose the fixed lower radial cutoff sufficiently small relative to the certified fixed inactive-bottom support. For both frequency signs, the exact floor-perturbed lower reciprocal antecedent B_low^pm equals the flat sharp cone B_flat^pm=sum_(d<=y)chi_4(d)sum_(h>=1)V_low(4R^2h^2/d^2)e(pm hX/d)/h plus O_epsilon(RX^epsilon). The proof retains every H_j, H_j+1, hard sample, profile star, and boundary; it uses Phi(u)-1=O(u^2), Phi'(u)=O(u), a uniform high-regularity weighted two-variable Fourier separation, and the accepted frequency-first theorem. Changing only the phase to N=floor X costs O(R). Fix J_(R,y)(t)=eta(yt)V_low(4R^2t^2)/t on the small positive arc, extended smoothly by zero and periodically. With A_y(m)=sum_(d<=y,d|m)chi_4(d) for all integer m including d|0, c_y=sum_(d<=y)chi_4(d)/d, and D_N(k)=sum_(d<=y)chi_4(d)(floor((N+k)/d)-floor(N/d)-k/d) for every integer k, exact Fourier completion and Abel summation give B_flat^(N)=sum_k D_N(k)(hat J_(R,y)(k)-hat J_(R,y)(k+1)). Hence the original lower owner is equivalent at the RX^epsilon scale to this prescribed-centre sharp truncated-character divisor discrepancy. The growing J seminorms supply no uniform estimate.
create.next_action: Prove one genuinely joint signed RX^epsilon bound for the exact sharp discrepancy wavelet, equivalently for the flat phase kernel. The interpolation seminorm, another invertible completion, or an outside absolute value is not a saving.

create.title: Global lower mod-four pairing and resonance-tubewise capacity obstruction
create.statement_tex: After exact profile-first aggregation and zero extension, adjacent odd pairing gives B_low^+=E_amp+K_X, where E_amp<<log^2 X and K_X=sum_(d=1 mod 4)sum_h b_X(h,d+2)e(hX/d)(1-e(-2hX/(d(d+2))))/h. For the flat cone E_amp<<log X. Thus the phase kernel is target-equivalent to the original lower antecedent. The sector ||2hX/(d(d+2))||<=R^(-1) is O(R log X), but local pairing does not control its complement. For infinitely many X=R^4, on d asymp R^2 and R^(4/5)<=h<=cR inside the lower support, disjoint tubes of width asymp R/sqrt(h) around the half-integer resonances 2hR^4/(d(d+2))=k+1/2 have fixed-sector phase and bracket; there are asymp h tubes per h, each of modulus >>R/h^(3/2), so the sum of tube moduli is >>R^(3/2). Therefore termwise, pairwise, or resonance-tubewise absolute summation cannot prove the RX^epsilon target. This is not a signed lower bound for the complete kernel; joint cancellation across heights and resonance labels remains open.
create.next_action: Freeze local mod-four pairing and resonance-by-resonance norms. Any continuation must retain the complete cross-height and cross-resonance signed sum until a quantified inequality is obtained.

reject.reason: Bare C1 regularity in two variables does not give an absolutely summable Fourier series. The valid proof uses the actual C-infinity multiplier and a weighted high-derivative Wiener estimate.
The graph certifies a fixed bottom-support constant. The proof chooses s_0 relative to that constant; a bare numerical edge may be used only with the exact profile certificate cited.
Flattening costs at most the target error but leaves the full flat signed cone. It is a bidirectional target-scale reduction, not an estimate of either main term.
The sample-exact cutoff changes between 0 and 1/y and has growing seminorms. Fixed-X Fourier convergence proves the identity only.
The bracket is maximal at half-integer increment resonances. Only the narrow integer-increment sector is target-safe by absolute values.
The R^(3/2) statement sums moduli after decomposing into tubes. Cancellation between tubes, labels, and heights remains available in the actual signed kernel.
The O(R) integerization changes only this reciprocal lower phase. It proves no uniform control of the separate endpoint operators or the full M9 bridge.
The completion globalizes the sharp denominator cutoff and full lower wavelet but returns to the accepted unmatched-crossing obstruction class without a quantitative inequality.
Even a future complete GAR theorem controls only the total active M1 aggregate and has no inverse implication to either literal blockwise M1 parent.

no_change.reason: Both direct blockwise parents remain open, and the alternative GAR route still lacks its lower signed estimate.
Its hard TOP, balanced, and unbalanced parents are independent and remain open.
Integerization of one lower reciprocal phase is not the separate endpoint-uniformity theorem.
M9-M1, M9-M2, and endpoint uniformity are not proved.
The new result is a target-scale equivalence and no-go, not a signed estimate below the accepted one-third menu frontier.
The lower GAR estimate, M9-M2, endpoint uniformity, and final bridge remain open; no quarter theorem or improved exponent follows.

round_assessment.reason: Round 121 proves that the entire literal lower profile/floor kernel is target-equivalent to one sharp cone and an exact all-integer truncated-character divisor-discrepancy wavelet. It also proves that local mod-four and resonance-tubewise norms retain R^(3/2) capacity. The signed discrepancy estimate, GAR, every M9 parent, and every exponent improvement remain open.
